answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by tying each active identity to a distinct cadastral parcel in a public ledger. A licensed surveyor records the parcel's boundary and mints one registration token; duplicates are rejected. Extra identities require extra parcels, each paying lease, survey, and audit cost C per epoch. With reward capped at R, n sybils earn n(R-C), so cloning pays only if R>C. The gale of demand and a zenith in land fees expose the shale parcel registry's weakness: colluding surveyors or forged deeds remain.
